ALL_PROXY.what: Standard proxy variable. Steam reads it with the other *_proxy variables to auto-detect proxy settings for its HTTP downloads (logged as "Auto-detected proxy settings: auto-detect, proxy, proxy-https, exclude"). Format is a URL such as http://host:port.

BREAKPAD_DUMP_LOCATION.what: Directory where Breakpad writes crash minidumps. Steam preallocates it in its process-environment manager and sets it for the CEF/steamwebhelper crash reporter; users can set it to redirect where minidumps land.

CEF_CRASH_REPORTER_PRODUCT_VERSION.what: Set by chromehtml.so before starting steamwebhelper so the CEF crash reporter tags its crash reports with the Steam client build/version.

CEF_CRASH_REPORTER_SERVER_URL.what: Set by chromehtml.so for steamwebhelper to https://crash.steampowered.com/submit, the endpoint the CEF crash reporter uploads web-helper crash dumps to.

CPU_MHZ.what: Fallback CPU clock speed in MHz, used by tier0 when it cannot read /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpufreq/cpuinfo_max_freq (the bootstrapper says "Try defining CPU_MHZ"). Set it to a number such as 3600 on systems without cpufreq.

DBG_PATHMATCH.what: Debug switch in the shared filesystem/path code. When set, the case-insensitive path-matching logic logs each step ("Matched '%s' -> '%s'", "Unmatched", "Lowered"), which helps diagnose files not found because of case differences.

DEBUGGER.what: Launches the legacy ubuntu12_32 client under the given debugger (special-cased values listed, anything else is used as a command prefix), disables srt-logger, and is unset for recursive launches; ignored on the steamrt64 path.

DEBUGGER_ARGS.what: Extra arguments passed to the debugger selected by DEBUGGER.

DEBUG_DRM.what: Debug switch read where Steam dynamically loads libdrm (drmGetDevices2, drmModeGetResources, ...), in steamui and streaming_client. Probably enables extra logging of DRM/KMS device enumeration.

DISPLAY.what: Standard X11 display name. Steam's UI, webhelper and streaming client connect to this X server; with STEAM_MULTIPLE_XWAYLANDS (gamescope) Steam also builds other display names in the form :N.

DONT_BREAK_ON_ASSERT.what: When set, failed asserts in Steam's tier0 code do not break into a debugger or show the assert dialog. steam.sh sets it to 1 for valgrind runs. Related to the -noassert command-line option.

DXVK_STATE_CACHE_PATH.what: DXVK's directory for its state cache. steamclient reads it when it prepares the per-app shader cache, and Steam points it at a DXVK_state_cache folder inside the app's shader-cache directory, creating the directory if needed.

ENABLE_VULKAN_RENDERDOC_CAPTURE.what: RenderDoc's Vulkan layer enable switch (1 = load the capture layer). steam-launch-wrapper can set it for a game, probably from the per-app environment files under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/steam/env/.

EnableConfiguratorSupport.what: Read by steamclient. The name matches the Steam Input setting that enables controller configuration support for each controller type (a bitmask). Probably an environment override for that setting.

FOSSILIZE_APPLICATION_INFO_FILTER_PATH.what: Path to a Fossilize application-info filter file that the Steam Fossilize Vulkan layer reads to decide which applications/engines to record pipelines for. If the file cannot be parsed, recording goes ahead anyway.

FOSSILIZE_DISABLE_RATE_LIMITER.what: Read by fossilize_replay. When set, it turns off the replayer's rate limiter, so background shader pre-compilation is not throttled (the same as --disable-rate-limiter).

FOSSILIZE_DUMP_SYNC.what: Read by the Steam Fossilize layer. When set, it probably writes recorded pipeline state to disk synchronously instead of from a background thread, which makes captures more reliable when a crash is expected.

FOSSILIZE_REPLAY_WRAPPER.what: Read by fossilize_replay. It names a wrapper program (for example a debugger or tracer) that the replayer re-execs itself through when it starts replay processes.

FOSSILIZE_REPLAY_WRAPPER_ORIGINAL_APP.what: Set by fossilize_replay when it re-launches itself through FOSSILIZE_REPLAY_WRAPPER, so the wrapped process knows the path of the original replayer binary. Internal.

GAMESCOPE_DISPLAY_DISABLED.what: Read by streaming_client next to GAMESCOPE_WAYLAND_DISPLAY. When set, the streaming client does not use gamescope's Wayland display for video output and falls back to its normal SDL/X11 window.

GAMESCOPE_MODE_SAVE_FILE.what: Listed as an environment read, but its strings sit among the gamescope X atoms, so it is probably really the gamescope root-window property of the same name. That property holds the path of the file where gamescope saves the user display-mode choices. Steam reads it in a gamescope session to manage saved resolution and refresh settings.

GAMESCOPE_WAYLAND_DISPLAY.what: Name of gamescope's private Wayland socket (for example gamescope-0), which gamescope exports. Steam uses it to detect a gamescope session, and the overlay and streaming client connect to it for gamescope_xwayland/dmabuf integration. Without it, Wayland init is skipped.

GDK_SCALE.what: GTK integer UI scale factor. The Steam vgui2 X11 surface reads it, together with the -display-scale= option, to choose the scale for legacy VGUI windows.

GLIBCXX_TUNABLES.what: libstdc++ tunables string that every binary reads through the statically linked C++ runtime, for example glibcxx.eh_pool.obj_size and obj_count to size the exception emergency pool. It is not a Steam-specific setting.

GLOVERLAYCOREPROFILE.what: Read by gameoverlayrenderer.so in its OpenGL path. When set, it probably forces the overlay to render with a shader/core-profile path instead of fixed-function. The overlay logs which mode it uses ("OpenGL version ... overlay will use %s").

HOME.what: User home directory. Steam uses it to find ~/.steam, ~/.local/share/applications (for desktop shortcuts) and, when XDG variables are unset, XDG user directories. Steam asserts if it cannot find a home directory.

HOMETEST_DESKTOP_SESSION.what: Test override for the desktop session name (default plasma) that steamui legacy "Switch to Desktop" path selects through steamos-session-select or the display manager D-Bus API, when SteamOS Manager is unavailable.

HOMETEST_DESKTOP_USER.what: Test override for the user account that steamui legacy "Switch to Desktop" path switches the session for (logged as "Switching to session %s for user %s"); used with HOMETEST_DESKTOP_SESSION when SteamOS Manager is unavailable.

HTTPS_PROXY.what: Standard HTTPS proxy URL. Steam reads it during proxy auto-detection and uses it as the proxy-https setting.

HTTP_PROXY.what: Standard HTTP proxy URL (http://host:port). Steam reads it during proxy auto-detection for its downloads and web requests.

IgnoreChildProcesses.what: Read by the game overlay. When set, the overlay probably does not inject into or attach to child processes of the game, and stays attached only to the original game process.

JPEGMEM.what: libjpeg's limit on memory use (for example 50M; the value is parsed as number plus K/M suffix). It is read by the libjpeg linked into Steam binaries; Steam itself does not use it.

LANG.what: Standard locale variable. Steam reads it for X input-method setup in vgui2 (XOpenIM), as the fallback locale, and in the hardware survey. Steam may also reset it to C/host values for games.

LC_ALL.what: Standard locale override. steamclient reads it when building a game's environment: the host value is kept as HOST_LC_ALL, and Proton/compat launches may get a Steam-chosen locale unless the app sets DisableLinuxLocaleOverride.

LD_LIBRARY_PATH.what: Rebuilt by steam.sh and the scout run.sh for the client; for games, non-scout entries are captured by _v2-entry-point into PRESSURE_VESSEL_APP_LD_LIBRARY_PATH and unset.

LD_PRELOAD.what: Moved into the gdb args file under gdb by steam.sh; for games captured by _v2-entry-point/pressure-vessel-unruntime and passed as --ld-preloads (overlay preloads handled specially).

MANGOHUD_CONFIGFILE.what: MangoHud config file path. On gamescope/Steam Deck, steamclient reads or sets it so that mangoapp (the performance overlay) uses Steam's generated config/mangohud.conf.

NO_PROXY.what: Comma-separated list of hosts or domains that bypass the proxy. Steam reads it as the "exclude" list during proxy auto-detection (each entry is matched as *%s).

OBJCOPY.what: Path to the objcopy tool (default <prefix>objcopy). steamclient and steamservice use it to add or remove ELF sections in binaries ("--add-section", "--remove-section"), probably when stamping or stripping signature data. Developer-only.

OPENSSL_ia32cap.what: OpenSSL's CPU-capability mask override. The OpenSSL statically linked into Steam reads it, so it can disable SIMD/AES-NI code paths when debugging crypto problems.

PATH.what: Executable search path. steam-launch-wrapper reads it and, when the game-bin option is on, prepends <dir>/game-bin to it before running the game ("Unable to set new PATH" on failure).

PRESSURE_VESSEL_SYSTEMD_SCOPE.what: steam-launch-wrapper sets it to 0 after it has placed the game in its own transient systemd scope, so pressure-vessel does not try to create another scope.

RADV_DEBUG.what: Mesa RADV debug flags (comma-separated). steamclient reads it when building the shader-pre-compilation (Fossilize replay) environment and appends ,nomemorycache, so the replay fills the on-disk cache instead of RADV's in-memory cache.

RADV_FORCE_VRS_CONFIG_FILE.what: Mesa RADV variable that names a file whose contents (1x1 or 2x2) set the forced variable-rate-shading rate. Steam (Deck dynamic VRS, STEAM_USE_DYNAMIC_VRS) writes 1x1 or 2x2 into that file at runtime to change the shading rate of running games.

SDL_APP_NAME.what: Steam sets it to 'Steam' (or the streaming client's name). SDL uses it as the application name that the audio server (PulseAudio/PipeWire) and the screensaver inhibitor show.

SDL_AUDIO_DEVICE_SAMPLE_FRAMES.what: The streaming client sets this hint to request an audio buffer size in sample frames, to keep Remote Play audio latency low.

SDL_AUDIO_DEVICE_STREAM_NAME.what: Name given to each audio stream in the sound server's mixer: 'Game streaming client (playback)' and '(microphone)' in the streaming client, and 'Audio recorder' for the recording or voice capture in steamui.

SDL_AUDIO_DEVICE_STREAM_ROLE.what: Media role given to Steam's audio streams. 'Game' is used for streamed game audio and 'GameChat' for microphone/voice, so PipeWire/PulseAudio policies can route or duck them.

SDL_ENABLE_GTK.what: steamui sets it to 0 before SDL_Init so SDL3 does not load or initialize GTK (used for tray/menu integration) inside the Steam process.

SDL_ENABLE_STEAM_CONTROLLER_MOUSE_MODE.what: Read by the SDL HIDAPI Steam Controller driver in streaming_client. When set, it leaves the Steam Controller's built-in mouse and keyboard emulation on instead of clearing the digital mappings.

SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG.what: SDL controller mapping database string. steamui reads and sets it to add Steam's own mappings (entries with crc and sdl://<index> identifiers) for controllers it hands to SDL.

SDL_GAMECONTROLLER_IGNORE_DEVICES.what: SDL list of controller VID/PID pairs to ignore (0xVID/0xPID, comma-separated). The overlay renderer reads it, probably so that the virtual Steam Input devices are hidden from the game.

SDL_JOYSTICK_GAMEINPUT.what: The streaming client sets it to 0, disabling SDL's Windows GameInput joystick backend. This only matters on Windows builds.

SDL_JOYSTICK_HIDAPI.what: The streaming client sets it to 1 so SDL uses its HIDAPI drivers to read controllers directly for Remote Play input.

SDL_JOYSTICK_HIDAPI_COMBINE_JOY_CONS.what: steamui sets it from the user's controller setting controller_combine_nintendo_joycons, to choose whether a left and right Joy-Con pair act as one controller.

SDL_JOYSTICK_HIDAPI_GAMECUBE.what: The streaming client sets it to 0 when streaming support for GameCube adapters is turned off ("Turning off streaming support for GameCube controllers"); the device is then shared over USB instead.

SDL_JOYSTICK_HIDAPI_JOYCON_HOME_LED.what: The streaming client sets it to 0 so SDL does not turn on the Joy-Con Home-button LED.

SDL_JOYSTICK_HIDAPI_PS4.what: The streaming client sets it to 0 when HIDAPI support for PS4 controllers is turned off for streaming, for example when the device is passed through via USB sharing instead.

SDL_JOYSTICK_HIDAPI_PS5.what: The streaming client sets it to 0 when HIDAPI support for PS5 controllers is turned off for streaming, for example when the controller is shared over USB instead.

SDL_JOYSTICK_HIDAPI_STEAM.what: The streaming client sets it to 0 so SDL's HIDAPI Steam Controller driver is not used. Steam itself owns Steam Controllers.

SDL_JOYSTICK_HIDAPI_STEAMXBOX.what: The streaming client sets it to 1, enabling SDL's HIDAPI driver for Steam's virtual Xbox-style controllers in the streaming client.

SDL_JOYSTICK_HIDAPI_SWITCH.what: The streaming client sets it to 0 when HIDAPI support for Nintendo Switch controllers is turned off for streaming, for example when they are shared over USB instead.

SDL_JOYSTICK_HIDAPI_XBOX.what: The streaming client sets it to 0 when HIDAPI support for Xbox controllers is turned off for streaming, for example when they are shared over USB instead.

SDL_KMSDRM_REQUIRE_DRM_MASTER.what: The streaming client sets it to 0 so SDL's KMSDRM video backend can start without DRM master. This lets it run on a console/VT, for example a Steam Link-style device, while another process owns the display.

SDL_MAC_REGISTER_ACTIVATION_HANDLERS.what: steamwebhelper sets it to 0 so SDL does not register macOS app-activation handlers. This has no effect on Linux; the code is shared with macOS.

SDL_MOUSE_AUTO_CAPTURE.what: steamwebhelper sets it to 0 so SDL does not grab the mouse automatically while a button is held over a browser window, which avoids stuck pointer grabs in Steam UI windows and context menus.

SDL_MOUSE_NORMAL_SPEED_SCALE.what: The streaming client sets it, as a float formatted %.2f, to scale absolute mouse motion according to the user's streaming mouse-speed setting.

SDL_MOUSE_RELATIVE_SPEED_SCALE.what: The streaming client sets it, as a float formatted %.2f, to scale relative (captured) mouse motion sent to the streamed game.

SDL_MOUSE_TOUCH_EVENTS.what: The streaming client sets it to 0 so SDL does not generate synthetic touch events from the mouse. Each input type is forwarded to the host as itself.

SDL_NO_SIGNAL_HANDLERS.what: steamui sets it to 1 so SDL does not install SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers; Steam handles signals itself.

SDL_OPENVR_CURSOR_WIDTH.what: The streaming client's OpenVR video mode sets it to 0.06, the size of the cursor drawn on the VR overlay panel.

SDL_OPENVR_INPUT_PROFILE.what: The streaming client's OpenVR mode sets it to its action manifest, resource/streaming_client/sdloverlay_actions.json, so VR controller input maps to the streaming overlay.

SDL_OPENVR_LIBRARY.what: In --openvr mode the streaming client sets it to libopenvr_api.so, the OpenVR library that SDL's OpenVR video driver loads.

SDL_OPENVR_OVERLAY_FLAGS.what: The streaming client's OpenVR mode sets it to the flags SDL applies to the VR overlay it creates for the stream. The value is not visible.

SDL_OPENVR_OVERLAY_NAME.what: The streaming client sets it to 'steamlink_openvr', the OpenVR overlay key/name for streaming a desktop or game into VR.

SDL_OPENVR_OVERLAY_PANEL_WIDTH.what: The streaming client sets it to 2.75, the width in meters of the VR overlay panel that shows the stream.

SDL_OPENVR_WINDOW_ICON_OVERRIDE.what: The streaming client sets it to false, so SDL's OpenVR driver keeps the default overlay thumbnail/icon instead of using the window icon.

SDL_PEN_MOUSE_EVENTS.what: The streaming client sets it to 0 so pen input does not also produce synthetic mouse events.

SDL_PEN_TOUCH_EVENTS.what: The streaming client sets it to 0 so pen input does not also produce synthetic touch events.

SDL_RENDER_DRIVER.what: The streaming client sets the SDL renderer from its options (--opengl, --opengles2, --d3d9 or --d3d11, defaulting to vulkan; opengles2 for OpenVR). Users can also set it to force a renderer. HDR output requires the Vulkan renderer.

SDL_RENDER_OPENGL_NV12_RG_SHADER.what: The streaming client sets it to 1 or 0 to choose the SDL GL shader path for NV12 video textures: an RG-format UV plane versus separate textures, depending on the EGL/dmabuf frame import.

SDL_SCREENSAVER_INHIBIT_ACTIVITY_NAME.what: Reason string SDL passes when it inhibits the screensaver (D-Bus inhibit). Steam uses 'Downloading', 'Game streaming (server)' or 'Game streaming client', so desktop power or idle UIs show why Steam keeps the screen awake.

SDL_TIMER_RESOLUTION.what: steamui and steamwebhelper set it to 0 so SDL does not raise the system timer resolution. This is Windows-only and has no effect on Linux.

SDL_TOUCH_MOUSE_EVENTS.what: The streaming client sets it to 0 so touches do not also generate synthetic mouse events; touch is forwarded to the host as touch.

SDL_TV_REMOTE_AS_JOYSTICK.what: The streaming client sets it to 0 so TV remotes (Android TV builds) are not exposed as joysticks.

SDL_VIDEODRIVER.what: SDL2 video driver; steam.sh and the bootstrapper rewrite an exact `wayland` to `wayland,x11` so X11 fallback is possible.

SDL_VIDEO_ALLOW_SCREENSAVER.what: steamui, steamwebhelper and gldriverquery set it to 1 so opening SDL windows does not disable the screensaver. Steam inhibits it explicitly only when needed, for example while downloading or streaming.

SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER.what: The streaming client sets the SDL video backend to x11, wayland, or openvr in --openvr mode. Users can set it in the environment to force a backend; steam.sh rewrites a plain 'wayland' to 'wayland,x11'.

SDL_VIDEO_FORCE_EGL.what: The streaming client sets it to 1 or 0, choosing EGL instead of GLX on X11 for its OpenGL renderers. EGL is needed for dmabuf/EGLImage zero-copy video frames.

SDL_VIDEO_MINIMIZE_ON_FOCUS_LOSS.what: steamwebhelper sets it to 0 so fullscreen Steam windows, such as Big Picture, are not minimized when they lose focus.

SDL_VIDEO_X11_NET_WM_BYPASS_COMPOSITOR.what: steamui and steamwebhelper set it to 0 so SDL does not ask the X compositor to unredirect Steam windows (_NET_WM_BYPASS_COMPOSITOR), which keeps transparency and compositing working.

SDL_VIDEO_X11_SCALING_FACTOR.what: Set to 1.0 by steamui and steamwebhelper so SDL itself does no X11 content scaling; Steam/CEF handle DPI scaling themselves.

SDL_VIDEO_X11_WINDOW_VISUALID.what: Set to a specific X visual ID (%lu) before window creation, so SDL creates the webhelper composer or streaming window with a visual that matches the GL/EGL config, for example an ARGB visual for transparency.

SDL_WINDOWS_DETECT_DEVICE_HOTPLUG.what: Set to 0 by steamui and steamwebhelper, which stops SDL's Windows device-hotplug window. This is Windows-only and has no effect on Linux.

SDL_WINDOWS_ERASE_BACKGROUND_MODE.what: steamwebhelper sets it to always or never, controlling whether SDL erases a new window's background on Windows. This is Windows-only and has no effect on Linux.

SDL_WINDOW_ACTIVATE_WHEN_SHOWN.what: steamwebhelper sets it to 0 so showing a Steam window does not steal focus. With multiple Xwaylands, Steam manages focus itself through XSetInputFocus.

SDL_WINDOW_RETAIN_CONTENT.what: steamwebhelper sets it to 1, a hint to keep window contents across hide and show or resize. It is related to the composer mode (OpenGL/Gamescope).

SDR_CERT.what: Steam Datagram Relay certificate for a hosted dedicated server. It must be set together with SDR_PRIVATE_KEY; setting only one of them is an error. Used when running a server behind Valve's relay network without Steam login.

SDR_CLIENT_PORT.what: Read by SteamNetworkingSockets (SDR client). Probably fixes the local UDP port that the client uses for relay traffic.

SDR_DEVTICKET.what: Developer/debug SDR authorization ticket (base64). When set, the client uses it to connect to a gameserver through Steam Datagram Relay instead of getting a real ticket. The ticket must match the remote host and the local identity.

SDR_IP.what: Public IPv4 address (or enable/auto) that a hosted dedicated server advertises for Steam Datagram Relay.

SDR_IP6.what: IPv6 counterpart of SDR_IP for hosted dedicated server SDR routing (address, enable or auto).

SDR_LISTEN_PORT.what: UDP port on which a hosted dedicated server listens for relayed SDR traffic. Use a number or 'any' (the OS chooses). It is required when SDR_POPID is set; otherwise the POP ID becomes 'err'.

SDR_NETWORK_CONFIG.what: Path to (or contents of) an SDR network config, the relay/POP list, for hosted dedicated servers. It lets the server start relay routing without downloading the config from Steam.

SDR_POPID.what: Valve data-center POP code (for example 'iad') where a hosted dedicated server is located. It must exist in the SDR network config, otherwise relayed traffic cannot be received. Requires SDR_LISTEN_PORT.

SDR_PRIVATE_KEY.what: Private key matching SDR_CERT for a hosted dedicated server on Steam Datagram Relay. Both must be set.

SDR_PROBE_RELAY_INTERVAL.what: Interval at which a hosted SDR server sends ping probes to relays (parsed as a number; "Failed to parse %s value" if invalid). Requires a signed cert.

SDR_PROBE_RELAY_INTERVAL_BUSY.what: Relay probe interval that a hosted SDR server uses while it is busy (has active traffic); the busy-state version of SDR_PROBE_RELAY_INTERVAL.

SESSION_MANAGER.what: X Session Management (XSMP) address. vgui2 reads it to connect Steam's legacy UI to the desktop session manager ("Could not connect to X session manager").

SITE_SERVER_GUI.what: Read by steamclient. When set, it probably enables the built-in SiteServerUI web interface (/siteserver/, /login routes) used for Steam cafe/site-license server administration.

SLEEP_BEFORE_ELEVATED_UPDATE.what: Debug switch for the bootstrapper. Before an elevated (admin) self-update it makes the process sleep ("pid %u sleeping...") so a debugger can attach. Mostly relevant on Windows.

SRT_LOG.what: Comma-separated debug-log flags for all steam-runtime-tools programs (upstream doc).

SRT_LOGGER.what: Path to the srt-logger executable used by logger-0.bash (default: next to logger-0.bash).

SRT_LOGGER_TIMESTAMPS.what: Whether srt-logger adds timestamps to logged lines.

SRT_LOGGER_USE_JOURNAL.what: Whether srt-logger also writes to the systemd Journal.

SRT_LOG_ROTATION.what: 0 disables log rotation in srt-logger (client console log) and acts like STEAM_LINUX_RUNTIME_KEEP_LOGS in _v2-entry-point.

SRT_LOG_TERMINAL.what: Terminal to which srt-logger mirrors output.

SRT_LOG_TO_JOURNAL.what: Send steam-runtime-tools diagnostics to the systemd Journal.

STEAMNETWORKINGSOCKETS_LOG_FILE.what: Path of a debug log for SteamNetworkingSockets in steamclient and streaming_client (default name steamnetworkingsockets.log). Use with STEAMNETWORKINGSOCKETS_LOG_LEVEL.

STEAMNETWORKINGSOCKETS_LOG_LEVEL.what: Numeric verbosity of the SteamNetworkingSockets debug log written to STEAMNETWORKINGSOCKETS_LOG_FILE.

STEAMOS.what: Set to 1 by steam.sh for -steamos/-steamos3 (can be preset); when non-empty the ldd missing-32-bit-library check is skipped (legacy path).

STEAMOS_STEAM_REBOOT_SENTINEL.what: Path of a sentinel file set by the SteamOS session. When Steam is asked to reboot, it writes this file and exits so the session wrapper performs the reboot ("Enabling SteamOS reboot workaround").

STEAMOS_STEAM_SHUTDOWN_SENTINEL.what: Path of a sentinel file set by the SteamOS session. On shutdown, Steam writes it and exits so the session wrapper powers off the machine ("Enabling SteamOS shutdown workaround").

STEAMVIDEOTOKEN.what: Token that steamwebhelper sets (through the process environment manager) to unlock licensed H.264/HEVC video decoding in CEF ("h264_unlock", steam_video_token). Internal; users should not set it.

STEAMVIDEOTOKEN2.what: Second video-unlock token that steamwebhelper sets to a fixed constant (7b7fe2a66d548a0daf01c44056f5) alongside STEAMVIDEOTOKEN, so the bundled CEF/ffmpeg allows proprietary codecs. Internal.

STEAMWEBHELPER_USE_TERMINAL.what: Any non-empty value makes ubuntu12_64/steamwebhelper.sh pass --terminal-level=debug to srt-logger so webhelper output also goes to the terminal (legacy client path, undocumented).

STEAM_ALLOW_DRIVE_ADOPT.what: Read by steamui's UDisks2 storage manager (SteamOS). It enables or disables "adopting" external drives as Steam library drives (logged as "Allow drive adopt: %d").

STEAM_ALLOW_DRIVE_UNMOUNT.what: Read by steamui's UDisks2 storage manager (SteamOS). It enables or disables unmounting drives from the Steam storage UI (logged as "Allow drive unmount: %d").

STEAM_BOOTSTRAP_LOG_VERBOSE.what: When set, the bootstrapper writes verbose update and unpack logging (each file deleted, folder created and package unzipped) to logs/bootstrap_log.txt.

STEAM_BROWSER_RESIZE_WORKAROUND.what: Read by steamwebhelper. It probably turns on a workaround for window-resize rendering glitches in the CEF browser windows.

STEAM_CEF_GPU_CMD_PREFIX.what: Developer switch. Its value is passed to steamwebhelper as --gpu-launcher='<value>', so the CEF GPU process starts under a wrapper or debugger (similar to the renderer gdb prefix used with STEAM_DEBUGCEF).

STEAM_CLIENT_CONFIG_FILE.what: Path to steam.cfg (bootstrapper inhibit settings, CMForce, ...). The bootstrapper and client read it to override the location, and Steam exports it to games as <steamroot>/steam.cfg.

STEAM_CLIENT_LOG_FOLDER.what: Name of the log directory under the Steam data dir (default logs). Client components, the webhelper and steamsysinfo write their log files there.

STEAM_CLOUD_GAMING_PLATFORM.what: Identifies the cloud-gaming host Steam is running on. Recognised values are Valve and NVIDIA (GeForce NOW); anything else logs "Unknown cloud gaming platform".

STEAM_COMPAT_LAUNCHER_SERVICE.what: Names a compat tool (for example proton or container-runtime) in which Steam starts steam-runtime-launcher-service, so developers can run commands inside the game's container or Proton environment. steamclient reads it and passes it on to the tool environment.

STEAM_COMPAT_MOUNTS.what: Colon-separated extra host paths that the pressure-vessel container should share with the game. Steam reads any user value and appends its own (for example library and tool paths) when it builds the compat environment.

STEAM_COMPAT_PROTON.what: Set to 1 by Steam when the selected compat tool is Proton. steamclient also reads it, together with STEAM_COMPAT_PROTON_SUPPRESS, to decide Proton-specific behaviour.

STEAM_COMPAT_PROTON_SUPPRESS.what: Read next to STEAM_COMPAT_PROTON. When set, it probably stops Steam from marking or treating the launch as Proton.

STEAM_COMPAT_TOOL_MAPPINGS.what: Read by steamclient while it loads local compatibility tools (compatibilitytools.d). It probably lets developers override the app-to-compat-tool mapping (normally stored in the CompatToolMapping config) from the environment.

STEAM_DEBUG.what: Any non-empty value makes steam.sh run `set -x` and trace the whole launcher script.

STEAM_DEBUGCEF.what: Developer switch for the Steam web UI. It adds --remote-debugging-port, disables the hang monitor and seccomp sandbox, and can run the CEF renderer under gdb, making steamwebhelper debuggable.

STEAM_DESKTOP_APP_AFFINITY_LIST.what: CPU-affinity list that tier0 and its helpers read for desktop (non-game) processes. Probably used on Steam Deck to keep Steam's own processes off the cores reserved for games.

STEAM_DISABLE_BROWSER_SHUTDOWN_WORKAROUN.what: When set, steamwebhelper skips its "safe browser shutdown workaround" (the same as -disable_safe_shutdown_workaround).

STEAM_DISABLE_LIBNM_IPV6_WORKAROUND.what: SteamOS network manager switch. When set, steamclient does not apply its libnm IPv6 workaround, which sets the IPv6 addr-gen-mode when configuring connections through NetworkManager (logged as "SetIPv6Config: IPv6 libnm workaround: %d").

STEAM_DISABLE_MANGOAPP_ATOM_WORKAROUND.what: gamescope/Steam Deck switch. When set, Steam stops using an X atom workaround to control the mangoapp performance overlay (logged as "Using mangoapp atom workaround: %d"). gamescope-session sets it on newer gamescope versions.

STEAM_DISPLAY_REFRESH_LIMITS.what: Minimum and maximum refresh rate as '<min>,<max>' in Hz (for example 40,60). gamescope-session sets it to tell Steam the range its refresh-rate slider and FPS limiter may use. Invalid values or min greater than max are rejected.

STEAM_ENABLE_AMD_LAYER.what: Read by steamclient while it builds the game launch environment, next to the overlay and Vulkan-layer variables. Probably enables an AMD Vulkan layer for the launched game.

STEAM_ENABLE_DYNAMIC_BACKLIGHT.what: Steam Deck/gamescope session switch that turns on dynamic backlight control in the client. gamescope-session sets it on supported hardware.

STEAM_ENABLE_FAN_CONTROL.what: SteamOS switch that turns on Steam's fan-control feature: the System\FanMode setting and the fan-mode selector. gamescope-session sets it on supported handhelds.

STEAM_ENABLE_SHADER_CACHE_MANAGEMENT.what: Controls the shader cache manager (pre-caching, Fossilize background processing). steamclient checks it with the convar, command-line and registry switches; a disabling value logs "Shader manager disabled by environment".

STEAM_ENABLE_VOLUME_HANDLER.what: SteamOS session switch. When set, steamui's CSystemAudioController handles the hardware volume keys and system volume itself (logged as "handle volume keys: %d").

STEAM_ENABLE_XCOMPOSITE_WORKAROUND.what: steamwebhelper switch (0/1, logged as "Setting xcomposite workaround enabled via env var"). It makes the webhelper capture window textures through an XComposite workaround, like -use_xcomposite_workaround.

STEAM_EXTRA_COMPAT_TOOLS_PATHS.what: Colon-separated list of extra directories that Steam scans for custom compatibility tools (Proton builds and so on), in addition to /usr/share/steam/compatibilitytools.d, /usr/local/share/steam/compatibilitytools.d and <steamroot>/compatibilitytools.d.

STEAM_FORCE_CLIENT.what: Persistently selects the client by deleting (ubuntu12_32/scout/ldlp) or creating (steamrt64/steamrt3c/steamrt) the $STEAMROOT/.steam-enable-steamrt64-client opt-in flag.

STEAM_FOSSILIZE_DUMP_PATH.what: Path prefix where the Steam Fossilize layer writes recorded Vulkan pipeline state (.foz) for the game. Steam sets it per app inside the shader cache, and the layer logs "Overriding serialization path".

STEAM_FOSSILIZE_DUMP_PATH_READ_ONLY.what: Path to an existing, read-only Fossilize database (for example Steam's downloaded pipeline cache). The layer reads it so pipelines that are already known are not recorded again.

STEAM_FOSSILIZE_IDENTIFIER_DUMP_PATH.what: Path where the Steam Fossilize layer writes only pipeline identifiers/hashes, not full state, so Steam can track which pipelines a game uses.

STEAM_FOSSILIZE_LAST_USE_TAG.what: Tag (a hex value) that the Steam Fossilize layer attaches to recorded pipeline usage so Steam can tell which pipelines were used most recently, probably for cache pruning.

STEAM_FOSSILIZE_PIPELINE_USE_DUMP_PATH.what: Path where the Steam Fossilize layer writes pipeline-usage records, meaning which pipelines were actually bound at runtime, as opposed to full pipeline state.

STEAM_FOSSILIZE_PRECOMPILE_QA.what: QA switch for the Steam Fossilize layer, read next to FOSSILIZE_DUMP_SYNC. Probably used to check that a game's pipelines were already pre-compiled by Steam's shader pre-caching.

STEAM_FOSSILIZE_REPLAY_WRAP.what: Developer override read by steamclient's shader-compile job. Its value probably prefixes or wraps the fossilize_replay command line, for example with a debugger or profiler, when Steam pre-compiles pipelines in the background.

STEAM_GAMESCOPE_DYNAMIC_FPSLIMITER.what: gamescope-session switch that tells Steam gamescope supports the dynamic FPS limiter, so Steam uses it for the frame-limit slider (logged as "Dynamic FPS limiter: %d").

STEAM_GAMESCOPE_DYNAMIC_REFRESH_IN_STEAM.what: gamescope-session capability flag. It tells Steam that gamescope supports changing the display refresh rate dynamically while the Steam UI is focused (see the GAMESCOPE_DYNAMIC_REFRESH_IN_STEAM atom).

STEAM_GAMESCOPE_NIS_SUPPORTED.what: gamescope-session capability flag. It tells Steam that gamescope supports NVIDIA Image Scaling, so the NIS scaling filter appears in the Quick Access scaling options.

STEAM_GAMESCOPE_VRR_SUPPORTED.what: gamescope-session capability flag. It tells Steam that gamescope supports variable refresh rate (adaptive sync), so the VRR toggle can be shown.

STEAM_GAMESERVER_A2S_INFO_STRICT_LEGACY_.what: Game-server switch. When set, steamclient's master-server updater answers A2S_INFO ("Source Engine Query") with the strict legacy protocol, probably without the newer challenge or extended fields.

STEAM_GAMESERVER_ADVERTISE_SDR_LOCATION.what: Game-server switch. When set, the server's heartbeat to the Steam master server also reports its SDR ping location, so matchmaking can estimate ping.

STEAM_GAMESERVER_PACKET_HANDLER_NO_IPC.what: Game-server switch. When set, the client game-server packet handler is probably used in-process instead of through the steamclient IPC pipe.

STEAM_GAMESERVER_RATE_LIMIT_200MS.what: Game-server switch. When set, it probably applies a rate limit of one reply per 200 ms per source to game-server query replies, to protect against floods.

STEAM_GAME_LAUNCH_SHELL.what: Shell that runs game launch command lines, including user launch options with %command% (default /bin/sh).

STEAM_GLCOMPOSER_USE_MAKECURRENT_LEGACY.what: steamwebhelper GL composer switch (0/1, default false, logged as "GLComposer: makecurrent legacy mode: env: %d"). It makes the composer use the older glXMakeCurrent behaviour, to work around driver issues.

STEAM_IGNORE_INDIRECT_RENDERING.what: When set, Steam's legacy VGUI surface no longer shows the warning "OpenGL GLX context is not using direct rendering" (useful with remote X or software GL).

STEAM_LAUNCH_WRAPPER_DEBUG.what: Boolean (default 0). It turns on steam-launch-wrapper debug output, like --debug.

STEAM_LAUNCH_WRAPPER_GAME_BIN.what: Boolean (default 1). When true, steam-launch-wrapper prepends <dir>/game-bin to PATH for the game; --no-game-bin turns this off.

STEAM_LAUNCH_WRAPPER_JOURNAL.what: Boolean (default 0). When true, steam-launch-wrapper sends the game's stdout and stderr to the systemd Journal under the identifier steam-app<ID>, like --journal.

STEAM_LAUNCH_WRAPPER_SCOPE.what: Boolean (default 0). When true, steam-launch-wrapper puts the game in a transient systemd user scope app-steam-app<ID>-<pid>.scope, like --scope. Steam's launch environment may set it.

STEAM_MANGOAPP_HORIZONTAL_SUPPORTED.what: gamescope-session capability flag. It tells Steam that mangoapp supports the horizontal (single-line) performance overlay layout (logged as "Using mangoapp horizontal: %d").

STEAM_MANGOAPP_PRESETS_SUPPORTED.what: gamescope-session capability flag. It tells Steam that mangoapp supports preset-based performance overlay levels (logged as "Using mangoapp presets: %d").

STEAM_MULTIPLE_XWAYLANDS.what: Set by gamescope-session when gamescope runs more than one Xwayland server. Steam then connects to the extra X displays (:N) as well as $DISPLAY, so it can manage games on other Xwaylands.

STEAM_NO_FAST_PPT.what: Steam Deck/amdgpu power switch read in the TDP-limit code. When set, Steam probably sets only the sustained power cap (power1_cap) and not the fast/boost PPT limit (power2_cap).

STEAM_OPENAL_SKIP_CAPTURE.what: When set, steamclient probably skips opening OpenAL capture (microphone) devices, which avoids audio-device probing problems.

STEAM_OVERLAY_DISABLE_WAIT_FOR_CEF_FRAME.what: Read by gameoverlayrenderer.so. When set, the game overlay probably stops waiting for a new frame from the CEF overlay UI before presenting, which cuts latency but may show stale overlay frames.

STEAM_OVERLAY_FRAME_TIME_LOGGING.what: When set, the game overlay renderer writes per-frame timing to its log, /tmp/gameoverlayrenderer.<pid>.log.

STEAM_OVERLAY_LOGGING.what: When set, the game overlay renderer, injected into games, writes a debug log to /tmp/gameoverlayrenderer.<pid>.log.

STEAM_OVERLAY_LOGGING_FLUSH.what: When set, the overlay renderer flushes /tmp/gameoverlayrenderer.<pid>.log after every write, so no lines are lost if the game crashes.

STEAM_OVERLAY_VULKAN_LAYER_FORCE_COMPUTE.what: Read by the Steam overlay Vulkan layer around swapchain creation and present. When set, the layer probably draws the overlay with its compute-shader path instead of the graphics path.

STEAM_OVERLAY_WINDOW_BLACKLIST.what: Read by gameoverlayrenderer.so at startup with the game IDs. It probably lists executables or windows the overlay must not attach to, similar to the built-in vrmonitor exclusion.

STEAM_RUNTIME.what: Path of the Steam Runtime in use, or empty/0. The bootstrapper uses it when re-executing between scout and steamrt3, the hardware survey reports "<Runtime disabled>" when it is off, and steam-launch-wrapper logs "STEAM_RUNTIME not in use". steam.sh unsets it on the steamrt3 path.

STEAM_RUNTIME_DIALOG_UI.what: External dialog program that steam-runtime-dialog uses if it passes --check-features.

STEAM_RUNTIME_LIBRARY_PATH.what: The Steam Runtime's library search path. steamclient reads it to build the game's LD_LIBRARY_PATH and LD_PRELOAD (adding gameoverlayrenderer.so) unless the overlay is suppressed.

STEAM_RUNTIME_LOGGER.what: Controls srt-logger capture of the client's output into logs/console-linux.txt. 0 disables it, which helps when attaching debuggers; the bootstrapper logs "enable configured via STEAM_RUNTIME_LOGGER".

STEAM_RUNTIME_PREFER_HOST_LIBRARIES.what: Deprecated and has no effect; scout run.sh only logs a deprecation warning for 0.

STEAM_RUNTIME_SCOUT.what: Location of the unpacked scout LDLP runtime (default ubuntu12_32/steam-runtime), read by steam.sh and steamwebhelper.sh and by pressure-vessel for scout-on-SLR games.

STEAM_RUNTIME_STEAMRT.what: Developer override for the steamrt3c (sniper-based) runtime directory, default <steamroot>/steamrt64/pv-runtime/steam-runtime-steamrt. The client, webhelper and helpers read it to locate the runtime.

STEAM_RUNTIME_STEAMRT_SDK_ROOT.what: SDK sysroot used by the developer wrapper `pv-run.sh --sdk` (default steamrt64/pv-sdk; SDK not shipped).

STEAM_RUNTIME_USE_LIBCURL_SHIM.what: 1 makes scout run.sh prepend libcurl_compat_{32,64} to the library path (defaulted to 1 under valgrind-family DEBUGGER); undocumented, legacy client path.

STEAM_RUNTIME_VERBOSE.what: Non-empty enables debug output from scout setup.sh and steam-runtime-dialog.

STEAM_SPEW_LEVELS.what: Debug switch for per-group log verbosity. Comma-separated 'group=consolelevel,loglevel' pairs (parsed as %[^=]=%d,%d); invalid specs and unknown groups are ignored with a warning.

STEAM_UPDATEUI_PNG_BACKGROUND.what: Path to a custom image for the bootstrapper's update/progress window, replacing the default tenfoot/resource/images/bootstrapper.jpg.

STEAM_USE_DYNAMIC_VRS.what: Steam Deck/gamescope session switch that enables dynamic variable-rate shading. Steam writes 1x1 or 2x2 into the file named by RADV_FORCE_VRS_CONFIG_FILE to change the shading rate of running games.

STEAM_USE_MANGOAPP.what: gamescope-session switch. It tells Steam to use mangoapp (MangoHud running as a gamescope overlay app) for the Quick Access performance overlay, driven by config/mangohud.conf (logged as "Using mangoapp: %d").

STEAM_USE_WPASUPPLICANT.what: SteamOS session switch read by steamui. It probably makes Steam's Wi-Fi management talk to wpa_supplicant directly instead of going through NetworkManager.

STEAM_VALGRIND.what: Extra arguments passed to valgrind when DEBUGGER=valgrind.

STEAM_VKOVERLAY_FORCE_YCBCR_SUPPORT.what: Read by the Steam overlay Vulkan layer. It forces the layer to treat VK_KHR_sampler_ycbcr_conversion as supported (and enables its dependencies), probably so overlay video and streaming frames in YCbCr formats can be sampled.

STEAM_ZENITY.what: Dialog binary used by steam.sh/steam_msg.sh and runtime unpack progress dialogs; steam.sh sets it to the host zenity or `zenity`, and steam-runtime-steamrt.sh prefers ~/.steam/root/steam-dialog and unsets it if it points into scout.

SUPPRESS_STEAM_OVERLAY.what: If it is set in the environment when Steam builds a launch, steamclient leaves gameoverlayrenderer.so out of LD_PRELOAD, which disables the in-game overlay for that launch.

SYSTEM_LD_LIBRARY_PATH.what: The host LD_LIBRARY_PATH that steam.sh saved before adding the runtime. steamclient reads it to restore the host library path for processes that must run outside the Steam Runtime.

SYSTEM_PATH.what: The host PATH that steam.sh saved before adding the runtime. steamclient reads it to build the PATH for launched games and shell commands.

SteamAppId.what: AppID of the game Steam is running. steamclient reads it (for example when writing steam_appid.txt for Steamworks), and steam-launch-wrapper uses it to name the systemd scope and journal identifier steam-app<ID>.

SteamDeck.what: Set to 1 when running on a Steam Deck/SteamOS session. Games can check it, and the overlay and steamclient read it to change behaviour on the Deck.

SteamDisableOverlayDPIScaling.what: When set, the in-game overlay does not scale its UI by display DPI (SetScaleFactors).

SteamEnv.what: Set to 1 in processes started by Steam. steamclient reads it when connecting to the global user, to know the process was launched from inside a Steam environment.

SteamGameId.what: Game ID (64-bit; for plain Steam apps it equals the AppID, and non-Steam shortcuts have larger IDs) of the running game. Steam sets it, and the overlay reads it to identify which game it is attached to. gamescope also uses it to map windows to apps.

SteamGamepadUI.what: Set to 1 when the game was launched from the Big Picture/Gamepad UI. The overlay renderer reads it to use the gamepad-UI overlay behaviour.

SteamNoOverlayUIDrawing.what: When set, the overlay renderer stays loaded but does not draw the overlay UI (logged as "SteamNoOverlayUIDrawing was set"), so hooks such as screenshots and FPS keep working without overlay rendering.

SteamOS.what: Set to 1 on SteamOS. steamclient reads it around the overlay-enabled checks to adjust overlay and platform behaviour.

SteamOverlayGameId.what: The game ID the overlay should present as. It is usually the same as SteamGameId, but differs for things like non-Steam shortcuts or tools. Steam sets it, and the overlay renderer reads it.

SteamOverlayUseXFilterEvent.what: When set, the overlay passes X key events through XFilterEvent (input-method filtering) before translating them to characters, which helps IME/compose-key input in the overlay.

SteamRealm.what: Steam realm, either the global Steam or Steam China. Steam sets it for child processes, and the overlay UI and launcher read it to choose realm-specific config file names and paths (for example local_<realm>.vdf).

SteamStreamingAllowGameVsync.what: Read by the overlay renderer while the game is being streamed (Remote Play). When set, the game's vsync is left on instead of being disabled for streaming.

SteamStreamingVideo.what: Set by Steam for games launched during a Remote Play/streaming session. The overlay renderer reads it to turn on frame capture for video streaming.

SteamStreamingVideoDisableVSync.what: Set during Remote Play streaming. The overlay renderer reads it to force the game's vsync off so captured frames are not limited by the host display.

SteamTenfoot.what: Set to 1 when the game was launched from Big Picture ("tenfoot") mode. steamclient reads it, probably so that nested launches inherit Big Picture behaviour.

SteamUniverse.what: Steam universe of the running client (Public, Beta, ...). Steam sets it for child processes, and the bootstrapper, overlay UI and client read it to choose universe-specific paths (for example ~/.steam/steambeta, local_<x>.vdf).

StreamForOpenVR.what: Read by the overlay renderer with the SteamStreaming* variables. When set, the game's frames are streamed for OpenVR/SteamVR (for example to a VR headset streaming session) and not for normal Remote Play.

TMPDIR.what: Standard temporary directory (default /tmp). Steam uses it for steamXXXXXX temp files, the webhelper's scoped_dir_steam* directories and GL composer debug frame dumps.

TZDIR.what: Standard timezone database directory. steamui reads it with /etc/localtime and /etc/timezone to work out the system timezone, probably for the SteamOS time zone settings.

USER.what: Current user name. tier0 and others read it, for example for per-user names of temp files, IPC objects or locks.

VR_CONFIG_PATH.what: OpenVR override for the directory that holds SteamVR config (instead of ~/.config/openvr). Steam reads it with VR_OVERRIDE and VR_LOG_PATH to find the active VR runtime.

VR_LOG_PATH.what: OpenVR override for the SteamVR log directory. Steam reads it with VR_OVERRIDE and VR_CONFIG_PATH.

VR_OVERRIDE.what: OpenVR override that names the VR runtime directory to use instead of the one registered in openvrpaths.vrpath. Steam reads it when it locates SteamVR.

WAYLAND_DISPLAY.what: Standard Wayland socket name. steamui and streaming_client check it, together with XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland, to detect a Wayland session; this affects things such as using DRM directly versus going through the compositor for game streaming and recording.

WSL_DISTRO_NAME.what: Set by Windows Subsystem for Linux. tier0 and others read it to detect that Steam is running under WSL.

XDG_CONFIG_HOME.what: XDG config directory (default ~/.config). Steam reads it to resolve XDG user directories (user-dirs.dirs) and other per-user config paths.

XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP.what: When equal to `gamescope`, steam.sh/steam_msg.sh only log messages instead of showing blocking zenity/xterm dialogs.

XDG_DATA_HOME.what: XDG data directory (default ~/.local/share). Steam writes game .desktop shortcuts and steam_icon_<appid> icons under it, in icons/hicolor/<size>/apps.

XDG_RUNTIME_DIR.what: Per-user runtime directory (/run/user/<uid>). steam-launch-wrapper uses it to reach the systemd user manager's private socket for scopes, and to read per-app environment files under steam/env/.

XDG_SESSION_TYPE.what: Session type (x11 or wayland). steamui and the overlay renderer check for 'wayland' to adjust behaviour in Wayland sessions.

_STEAM_SETENV_MANAGER.what: Internal handshake for Steam's CProcessEnvironmentManager, which preallocates environment slots (BREAKPAD_DUMP_LOCATION, STEAMVIDEOTOKEN, overlay layer switches, ...) in the main process so that loaded DLLs can update them safely. If it is set from outside, the manager disables itself ("disabled by external environment setting"); users should not set it.

all_proxy.what: Lowercase spelling of ALL_PROXY. Steam checks both when auto-detecting the proxy for its HTTP traffic.

breakpad_testfile.what: Debug switch read by crashhandler.so while installing the Breakpad exception handler; probably makes it write a test minidump/file to verify crash reporting works. Value format unknown.

breakpad_verbose.what: Debug switch for crashhandler.so. When set, the Breakpad handler prints verbose trace messages ("Writing", "Skipping, no context", filter-callback messages) while handling a crash.

fs_debug.what: Debug switch for filesystem_stdio and the bootstrapper. When set, it probably logs file-system access or writes a batch-style debug script (the nearby strings are '@echo off ... set fs_target'). Mostly a Windows leftover.

http_proxy.what: Lowercase spelling of HTTP_PROXY. Steam checks it during proxy auto-detection.

https_proxy.what: Lowercase spelling of HTTPS_PROXY. Steam checks it during proxy auto-detection.

no_proxy.what: Lowercase spelling of NO_PROXY: the proxy bypass list Steam reads during proxy auto-detection.

steam_master_ipc_name_override.what: Overrides the name of the Steam master IPC pipe (default Steam3Master) that steamui and steamclient use to connect to the running Steam instance. It is read and set internally, so a second client or test harness can use a separate IPC namespace.
